newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee called to open 2.00 cents higher.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee called to open 2.00 cents higher.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures were called to open 2.00 cents higher Friday as traders expect a bounce back after Thursday's sell-off to 10-week lows.

But some traders doubted the market would make its pre-opening call, saying prices were likely to come in closer to unchanged. They said sentiment on the floor was still bearish, with some traders expecting to see follow-through selling and a test of yesterday's lows.
"It's called 2.00 higher, but there is no paper," said one trader. "If the specs come in again and drop the ball we'll go lower. Their recent behavior has been to sell."

Thursday, New York arabica futures fell sharply, battered by technically driven speculative and local selling. September settled down 13.40 cents at 166.10 cents a lb, its lowest settlement since April 15, after ranging from 181.00 to 165.00. Spot July finished 9.75 cents lower at 190.25, while the outer months fell 1.90 to 11.15.
The July/September switch bulged to 24.15 cents, from 19.85 cents at the close on Wednesday, while September/December narrowed to 19.85 cents compared with 22.75 cents.
On the charts, traders said the September contract faced resistance at 175.00 cents and then 180.00 cents. Support was seen at Thursday's low of 165.00 cents.
On the weather front, no damaging cold is expected in the next seven days in Brazil's coffee belt, U.S.-based forecaster Weather Services Corp said on Friday.
After Thursday's close, CSCE reported certified coffee stocks rose by 246 60-kg bags as of June 25, to 46,173 bags. There were 11,695 bags pending grading, the exchange said.
London robusta futures were expected to open down $100 on Friday, but came in some $31 lower. At the midday break, benchmark LIFFE September was off $41, to $1,760.
